title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 130) reopens the Fermat tower in the setting of the 'Longue Marche' continuation. Grothendieck says he wants to isolate a general situation that was only implicit in section 110).

General data:
- A group Γ acts on a connected, locally connected topos 𝒳 equipped with a geometric point x0.
- In the intended case, Γ = Γ_Q × S_3, identified with N_{0,3}, the 'arithmetic modular' group of the tripod.
- 𝒳 is the geometric tripod P^1_{Q̄} − {0,1,∞}. He writes it as a (universal-curve) version of M_{0,3} over Q̄, ≅ M_{0,4}.
- The base point is the tangential point 01 (with an arrow over it), with values in Q̄.

Definitions (278):
- Π = π1(𝒳, x0).
- 𝓜 = π1(𝒳, Γ; x0), the equivariant fundamental group, i.e. π1 of the quotient stack [𝒳/Γ].
- M = Π^ab = Π/[Π,Π].
- 𝓜̃ = 𝓜/[Π,Π]. This makes sense because [Π,Π] is characteristic in Π, hence normal in 𝓜.

This gives the morphism of extensions (279): 1→Π→𝓜→Γ→1 maps onto 1→M→𝓜̃→Γ→1, by epimorphisms on the first two terms and the identity on Γ.

He remarks that M could be replaced by any Γ-stable quotient of π^ab. For the Fermat curve of degree n this would be (Z/n)^2, or its profinite limit Ẑ^2.

He then introduces the universal abelian cover 𝒳'_0 = (universal cover)/[Π,Π], a principal M-cover of 𝒳.

The next page states the problem being set up:
- Classify the liftings of the Γ-action on 𝒳 to an action on 𝒳'_0 that is compatible with the action of Γ on the structure group M.
- More generally, do the same for any M-torsor 𝒳' obtained from 𝒳'_0 by twisting with an M-torsor E (the fibre at x0).

In modern terms:
- 𝓜̃ itself acts canonically on 𝒳'_0.
- Γ-liftings correspond to sections of 𝓜̃→Γ, up to M-conjugacy.
- Hence existence is governed by the class of the extension in H^2(Γ, M). Liftings, when they exist, form a torsor under (a quotient of) H^1(Γ, M) or Z^1(Γ, M).
- Twisting by E shifts things by the image of H^0/H^1 data.

The Γ_Q-part of this is the Galois action on the Fermat tower (Ihara's Ẑ^2-tower, Anderson, Coleman, Deligne: Jacobi sums, Ihara power series). The S_3-part encodes the symmetries of the Fermat curves permuting {0,1,∞}.

The marginal note appears to flag the hypothesis needed: 'discrete connectedness / 𝒳 locally simply connected in the profinite sense'.
errors: No substantive error. The notation 'M_{0,3} ≃ M'_{0,4}' is loose: M_{0,3} is a point, so what is meant is the universal curve over M_{0,3} (the tripod), i.e. M_{0,4} ≅ P^1−{0,1,∞}.

S_3 does not fix the tangential point 01, so 𝓜→Γ need not split over S_3. That is why the existence of liftings is a genuine problem, which Grothendieck treats correctly by working with the equivariant π1 and an abstract geometric point rather than assuming a section.

The marginal hypothesis (local simple connectedness in the profinite sense) is needed for the universal cover, and hence the quotient by [Π,Π], to exist as a topos-theoretic object. For the tripod this is harmless.

ideas.what: Equivariant fundamental group π1(𝒳,Γ;x0) of a topos with a group action, as an extension of Γ by π1(𝒳,x0)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the quotient stack [𝒳/Γ]; homotopy exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 exact sequence; equivariant/stack π1 in SGA1 and later topos-theoretic work)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (exact sequence of π1); the use of stacks M_{g,n} in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Pushing the extension 1→Π→𝓜→Γ→1 out along Π→Π^ab (or a Γ-stable quotient) to get the 'metabelian' extension 𝓜̃
ideas.modern_name: pushout of extensions; metabelian quotient of the arithmetic fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Ann. Math. 1986, Galois representation on the Fermat Ẑ^2-tower); Anderson; Coleman

ideas.what: Problem of lifting the Γ = Γ_Q × S_3 action from P^1−{0,1,∞} to the universal abelian (Fermat) cover and its twists by M-torsors, compatible with the action on the structure group
ideas.modern_name: equivariant structures on torsors; splittings of extensions, with obstruction in H^2(Γ,M) and classification by H^1(Γ,M)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard non-abelian cohomology (Giraud); for Fermat curves, Ihara and Anderson

ideas.what: Identification Γ_Q × S_3 = N_{0,3} as the arithmetic modular group acting on the tripod
ideas.modern_name: automorphism group of the tripod including the S_3 symmetries (Teichmüller tower level 0,3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); Ihara; Drinfeld (S_3-symmetry relations in GT)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the tripod and the Teichmüller tower, but not this notation explicitly

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a systematic study of S_3 × Γ_Q-equivariant structures on the whole Fermat tower and its torsor twists, as a general lifting problem for actions on abelian torsors over a topos. The Galois-only version is well studied (Ihara, Anderson, Coleman). An explicit treatment of the joint S_3 × Γ_Q lifting problem, in terms of an H^2 obstruction and H^1 torsor classification with tangential base points, is less standard. This is only the setup, though, so novelty is minor.
missed.quote: Commençons par dégager une situation typique générale, qui était un peu embrouillée entre les lignes dans 110).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to the S_3-equivariant description of the metabelian Galois representation (Ihara's power series and its symmetry relations, which are the abelianized shadow of the GT relations). These pages could show how Grothendieck intended to derive such relations independently, before Drinfeld and Ihara.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a general, essentially routine setup (an equivariant π1 extension, pushed out to the abelianization, plus a lifting problem for the universal abelian cover). Its interest is historical: Grothendieck independently framing the Galois action on the Fermat tower together with S_3 symmetry, parallel to Ihara's work. No new result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ_Q × S_3 } = N_{0,3}': the brace is probably a stray mark or '≃'; read 'Γ_Q × S_3 = N_{0,3}'.
'M_{0,3 Q̄}': the symbol has a hat or bar decoration (likely the universal curve over M_{0,3}), identified with M_{0,4} over Q̄.
Last line 'de groupe M les' is cut off; it continues onto the next page ('de proposer d'examiner…'), so likely 'de groupe M. Il est naturel / Il s'agit de proposer…'.
Marginal oblique note: probably 'connexité discrète (𝒳 loc. simpl. connexe au profini) suffit' or 'revient…'; it is attached to (278).
'(Au lieu de prendre M = Π/[Π,Π] = π_ab, on aurait pu prendre un quotient de π_ab invariant par action de Γ, mais peu importe...)': the deleted word is 'Considérons'.
